partnershipPlan: Two patient partners from the joint replacement class review the review questions and the plain-language summary; the digital services team advises on mobile coverage; physiotherapists comment on the workload findings before the committee meets.
socialListening: No social media listening; the centre's patient feedback forms from the last year are read for comments on activity monitoring and home exercise.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Seeing the numbers go up each week kept me going, especially when the physio sent a message.
items.implication: Report whether trials used named physiotherapist messages or automated targets.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: On the days my knee swelled I barely walked, and the watch made me feel I was failing.
items.implication: Extract whether step targets could be adjusted and whether trials reported harms such as distress.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Dad does not have a smartphone; we would have to set it up for him and we live an hour away.
items.implication: Record whether trials required a smartphone and what support they gave.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Three minutes a patient sounds small until there are forty patients on the dashboard.
items.implication: Present physiotherapist time per 150 active patients, not per patient.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Half the valley has no signal; the devices will only sync when people come into town.
items.implication: Flag evidence from areas with poor coverage and consider clinic synchronisation.

summary: Five composite voices on encouragement, targets, technology access, clinic time and coverage.
